chunks: And Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja‘far al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad Abū ‘Abdillāh al-Barqī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī al-Washshā, from ‘Alī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'How should we say salām to the people of the graves?' He replied: 'Yes, you say: Peace be upon the people of the dwellings, from among the believers and the believing women, and the Muslims and the Muslim women. You are forerunners for us, and we shall follow you, if God wills.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الدِّيَارِ: People of the dwellings (a common epithet for the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct formula for saying salam to the dead in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Kamil al-Ziyarah establishes the theological basis for addressing the deceased as 'people of the dwellings' (ahl al-diyaar), a phrase rooted in Quranic tradition to emphasize their continued spiritual presence. It highlights the Shia concept of the 'barzakh' as a transitional state where the living are 'forerunners' (farat) who will inevitably join the deceased, reinforcing the continuity of the believer's journey beyond death.
